newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND THANKS FINLAND FOR SECURITY MEDIATION ROLE.
newsitem.headline: POLAND THANKS FINLAND FOR SECURITY MEDIATION ROLE.

text.p: Poland's president thanked his visiting Finnish counterpart Martti Ahtisaari on Tuesday for his country's role in mediating disputes between Russia and NATO over the western military alliance's planned expansion.
"We appreciate Finland's role on the path of reconciling differing concepts of European security," President Aleksander Kwasniewski said after meeting Ahtisaari at the start of a three-day visit.

Last month Helsinki hosted a U.S.-Russia summit, which opened the way for the planned signing of a charter between NATO and Moscow defining new mutual relations before the pact's recruitment of new members from eastern Europe.

Poland, which hopes to be in the first batch of new NATO members along with the Czech Republic and Hungary around 1999, believes the summit brought it closer to NATO membership even though it did not dispel Russia's opposition to the process.

Ahtisaari, who gave strong assurances of Finland's support for Warsaw's efforts to join the European Union, said that even though his country remained neutral it respected Poland's right to join any security system it wished.
"Every country must be able to decide about its own security arrengements," he said at a news conference with Kwasniewski.
Ahtisaari promised that Finland, a fresh EU member, would lend Poland its expertise in adjusting its economy and regulations to Western standards.

The two presidents agreed to boost economic links and find ways to reduce Poland's trade deficit with Finland, which was $295 million last year. In 1996, Poland's exports to Finland shrank by 11 percent to $315 million while imports rose by 13 percent to $610 million.
Ahtisaari also said Finland would organise a conference this year of the Baltic region countries' border guards to step up the fight against mounting international crime.

Ahtisaari was scheduled to address the Polish parliament's foreign relations committeee later on Tuesday and meet Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz on Wednesday. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
